hook.title: Same signals as Solid. `renderToString` up to 4.7× faster.
hook.lede: If you know Solid, you know Pyreon: compiled JSX, signals, components that run once. Pyreon adds the rest of the stack in one box (router, forms, query, the Zero meta-framework) and compiles the same components to SwiftUI and Jetpack Compose (experimental).

proof.label: faster `renderToString` on a card component: 8.95M against 1.91M renders a second, byte-identical HTML enforced
faster on the other three server scenarios: a 50-row list, a 1,000-row list and a layout with component children
faster clearing 1,000 rows: 130 µs against 460 µs
proof.condition: real Chromium, run 1 table of a two-run record

table.title: Pyreon and Solid, line by line.
table.note: Solid is the closest relative Pyreon has, and it wins four of the measured rows below. Synthetic, author-run, Apple M3 Max, real Chromium unless noted. Reproduce: pyreon.dev/docs/benchmarks

rows.rival: Slower in all four; HTML is byte-identical (one run, bun)
870 / 880 µs; a tie in run 1, Pyreon 1.10× in run 2, so not claimed
3.06 / 3.10 ms: Solid 1.15–1.18× faster in both runs
7.5 KB: the smallest framework in the record
45 / 40 µs: Solid 1.11–1.13× faster (one 5 µs clock quantum)

rows.pyreon: `<For each={rows} by={(r) => r.id}>`: an explicit key function.
rows.rival: `<For>` keys by item identity; `<Index>` by position.

rows.pyreon: Router, query, forms, store, i18n, charts and the Zero meta-framework, all signal-native.
PMTC compiles the same components to SwiftUI and Compose (experimental).

rows.rival: A stable 1.x with years of production use.

code.title: The same search box, twice.
code.caption: Read the two side by side: they are almost the same program. The differences are the signal shape and the `by` key on `<For>`.

rival.label: Solid 1.9

pyreon.label: Pyreon

code.checked: Solid side: typechecked against solid-js 1.9.17 under `tsc --strict`. Pyreon side: typechecked against the repo's `tsconfig` (0 errors), compiled with the real JSX compiler (`transformJSX`) and mounted in happy-dom; typing into the input filters the list.

pickTheOther.title: When to pick Solid
items: Bundle size is the deciding number: the same app is 7.5 KB in Solid and 17.2 KB in Pyreon.
Your pages mount deep component trees and that cost dominates: Solid is 1.15–1.18× faster there.
You want a stable 1.x API with a long production record.

migrate.title: Bring your Solid code with you.
migrate.text: `@pyreon/solid-compat` runs `createSignal`, stores, resources and the control-flow components. Convert to Pyreon's own API file by file.
